item.title: Making myself design a PCB for the comma.ai Challenge in under 24 Hrs
item.description:
After taking a slight fork in the road, I decided to return once again to pcb work, something I'm not fully competent in (yet). Coincidentally, comma.ai released a challenge so I decided to test my boundaries and hopefully figure out what I need to work on.

If you don’t know them, (pull up a browser now), comma.ai is a pioneering ai and self-driving company run by George Hotz, whom is also known for various “hacks”. They’ve made Openpilot, a L2 operational self driving software that is a really nice open-source version of the things that other automotive manufacturers keep behind closed doors.

item.title: About
item.description:
Hi! I’m John Hu, a third year Electrical Engineering student @ Duke with strong interests in EVs, power electronics, and analog circuit design. I currently act as the club president for Duke Hyperloop, where I lead, organize, and work with a team of students to make a concept Hyperloop system.

Projects

Scara Robot Arm

Designed and built a small-scale SCARA robot arm with a 5:1 reduction.

  • Shoulder: NEMA 17 stepper with a GT2 timing belt
  • Z-axis: lead screw and a second NEMA 17
  • Arm: pancake NEMA 17
  • Controls: Arduino Uno and a CNC shield
  • Modeled in Fusion 360, printed in PLA, iterated on tolerances

Miniature Cycloidal Drive

Designed and built a small-scale cycloidal drive using Fusion 360, PLA prints, and AliExpress ball bearings. The goal is a compact, high-ratio gearbox for robotics without relying on off-the-shelf planetary stages. Bench testing (torque and backlash) is still in progress.

item.title: Building a BT macropad with the nRF52840Plus
item.description: I was interested in working with BT and NFC so what better way to experiment than to make a small keyboard. In the last iteration of my adventure with keyboards, I routed a ATMEGA328P by myself with no status LEDS, way to debug anything besides tracing with a multimeter so I resolved to create a working circuit board this time with some more proper documentation.
